stem.en: West Asia has the oldest traces of cultivation, yet historians think that rice farming on the Yangtze was a separate beginning. What is the best reason?

text.en: Rice is a different plant from wheat and barley, and it grew wild in that part of the world.
The Yangtze dates are thousands of years later than West Asia's, and a spread cannot take that long.

feedback.en: A slow spread can take thousands of years, so a gap in dates does not settle the question.

text.en: The people of south China and West Asia never met.

feedback.en: The chart does not tell us this. Whether people met is hard to know. The plants are the stronger clue.

text.en: Farming was impossible in West Asia, so it had to begin elsewhere.

feedback.en: West Asia is on the chart as a farming region with wheat and barley.

explanation.en: Rice is a local plant of that region, not a copy of wheat. Different local plants make separate beginnings likely, though not certain: the idea of farming could still have travelled.

hints.en: Think about what the farmers were growing, not when.
